atoms.text: This guide configures the QueryLoom batch engine to read Parquet input files and write query results in the same account. The engine runs under an IAM role named queryloom-batch-role in account 111122223333. The bucket, analytics-input-prod, is in the same account, so no cross-account trust is involved. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::analytics-input-prod/warehouse/* and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with a prefix condition of warehouse/. In the same policy, allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::analytics-input-prod/results/* so the engine can write result files. Do not edit the bucket policy; the identity-based policy alone grants access because the role and the bucket share an account. Submit a test query that scans one partition and writes a result set. Then confirm that an object appears under results/ and that the request is logged under the role's session name.

This guide configures the QueryLoom batch engine to read Parquet input files and write query results across an account boundary. The engine runs under an IAM role named queryloom-batch-role in account 111122223333. The bucket, analytics-input-prod, is owned by account 444455556666, so the bucket owner must grant access explicitly. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement that names arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/queryloom-batch-role as the principal and allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::analytics-input-prod/warehouse/* and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with a prefix condition of warehouse/. The same statement allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::analytics-input-prod/results/* so the engine can write result files. The role's own account must also permit these actions in its policy, but the grant on the bucket comes from the bucket policy. Submit a test query that scans one partition and writes a result set. Then confirm that an object appears under results/ and that the request is logged under the role's session name.

This guide gives the LogHarbor ingestion job access to read raw log archives and write compacted output, all in one account. The job assumes an IAM role named logharbor-compactor in account 111122223333. The bucket, ops-logs-archive, belongs to that same account. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on the raw/ prefix. Add s3:PutObject for the compacted/ prefix in that same policy so the job can write gzip-compressed output files. The bucket policy stays unchanged, because the role's identity-based policy is the only source of the grant. Set the job's input path to s3://ops-logs-archive/raw/ and its output path to s3://ops-logs-archive/compacted/. Run the job against one day of logs and verify that the compacted files appear with the expected object count. Check the access logs to confirm that every request came from the logharbor-compactor role.

This guide gives the LogHarbor ingestion job access to read raw log archives and write compacted output across two accounts. The job assumes an IAM role named logharbor-compactor in account 111122223333. The bucket, ops-logs-archive, is owned by account 444455556666, which must add the permissions on its side. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement with account 111122223333 as the principal, scoped by a condition to that role, allowing s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on the raw/ prefix. The same statement allows s3:PutObject for the compacted/ prefix so the job can write gzip-compressed output files. The role's account must also allow these actions in its own policy, but the bucket policy carries the grant on the bucket side. Set the job's input path to s3://ops-logs-archive/raw/ and its output path to s3://ops-logs-archive/compacted/. Run the job against one day of logs and verify that the compacted files appear with the expected object count. Check the access logs to confirm that every request came from the logharbor-compactor role.

This guide allows the PipeRiver ETL scheduler to read CSV drops and write cleansed partitions within a single account. The scheduler runs as an IAM role named piperiver-etl-exec in account 111122223333. It reads vendor files from the incoming/ prefix of the bucket sales-ingest-stage, which is in the same account. Create an identity-based policy for the role that allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket for incoming/. Extend the policy with s3:PutObject for cleansed/dt=*/ so each run can write date-partitioned output. Leave the bucket policy as it is; no bucket-level statement is needed because the role and the bucket share an account. Configure the scheduled pipeline with incoming/ as its source and cleansed/ as its sink. Trigger a manual run with a sample file of 10,000 rows. Verify that a partition for the current date is created and that the row count matches the source.

This guide allows the PipeRiver ETL scheduler to read CSV drops and write cleansed partitions when the bucket is in another account. The scheduler runs as an IAM role named piperiver-etl-exec in account 111122223333. It reads vendor files from the incoming/ prefix of the bucket sales-ingest-stage, which is owned by account 444455556666. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement naming arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/piperiver-etl-exec as the principal, allowing s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket for incoming/. The same statement allows s3:PutObject for cleansed/dt=*/ so each run can write date-partitioned output. The role's own account must permit the same actions, while the bucket policy supplies the cross-account grant. Configure the scheduled pipeline with incoming/ as its source and cleansed/ as its sink. Trigger a manual run with a sample file of 10,000 rows. Verify that a partition for the current date is created and that the row count matches the source.

This guide covers access for the MetricLattice aggregation job, which reads event JSON and writes hourly aggregates in one account. The job uses an IAM role named metriclattice-agg in account 111122223333. The event bucket, telemetry-events-core, is in that same account. Attach a policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject on events/year=*/month=*/* and s3:ListBucket on the bucket with a prefix condition of events/. Add s3:PutObject on aggregates/hourly/* in the same identity-based policy. The bucket policy is not modified, since the role's own policy provides all the access the job needs. Set the job's lookback window to 24 hours and its output location to aggregates/hourly/. Run it once and compare the aggregate record counts against a manual count of the input events. Review the role's access log entries to confirm that no requests were denied.

This guide covers access for the MetricLattice aggregation job, which reads event JSON and writes hourly aggregates across accounts. The job uses an IAM role named metriclattice-agg in account 111122223333. The event bucket, telemetry-events-core, is owned by account 444455556666. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement that names account 111122223333 as the principal, limited by a condition to the metriclattice-agg role, and allows s3:GetObject on events/year=*/month=*/* and s3:ListBucket with a prefix condition of events/. The statement also allows s3:PutObject on aggregates/hourly/*. The role's account must allow these actions too, but the grant on the bucket originates in the bucket policy. Set the job's lookback window to 24 hours and its output location to aggregates/hourly/. Run it once and compare the aggregate record counts against a manual count of the input events. Review the role's access log entries to confirm that no requests were denied.

This guide sets up the SQLRelay ad hoc query service to read datasets and write result sets and temporary spill files in one account. The service runs as an IAM role named sqlrelay-query in account 111122223333. The datasets are in the bucket research-datasets, which is in the same account. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on the curated/ prefix. Add s3:PutObject and s3:GetObject on the query-output/ prefix so the service can write results and read back spilled intermediate data. No change is made to the bucket policy, because the identity-based policy is the sole grant. In the service settings, set the result location to s3://research-datasets/query-output/. Run a query that joins two curated tables and exceeds the memory limit so that spill files are created. Confirm that the result file and the spill files appear under query-output/.

This guide sets up the SQLRelay ad hoc query service to read datasets and write result sets and temporary spill files across accounts. The service runs as an IAM role named sqlrelay-query in account 111122223333. The datasets are in the bucket research-datasets, which is owned by account 444455556666. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement naming arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/sqlrelay-query as the principal, allowing s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on the curated/ prefix. The statement also allows s3:PutObject and s3:GetObject on the query-output/ prefix so the service can write results and read back spilled intermediate data. The role's account must permit the same actions, but the bucket policy provides the grant for this bucket. In the service settings, set the result location to s3://research-datasets/query-output/. Run a query that joins two curated tables and exceeds the memory limit so that spill files are created. Confirm that the result file and the spill files appear under query-output/.

This guide grants the StreamMerge compaction service access to merge small objects into larger files in one account. The service runs under an IAM role named streammerge-worker in account 111122223333. It reads many small Avro files from the landing/ prefix of the bucket clickstream-landing, which is in the same account. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket for landing/. Add s3:PutObject for merged/ so the service can write consolidated files of roughly 256 MB. The bucket policy is left untouched; the role's policy alone authorizes the reads and the writes. Set the service's target file size to 256 MB and its source prefix to landing/. Start a compaction run on one hour of data. Verify that the number of objects under merged/ is lower than under landing/ and that the total record count is unchanged.

This guide grants the StreamMerge compaction service access to merge small objects into larger files across accounts. The service runs under an IAM role named streammerge-worker in account 111122223333. It reads many small Avro files from the landing/ prefix of the bucket clickstream-landing, which is owned by account 444455556666. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement that lists account 111122223333 as the principal, with a condition restricting it to the streammerge-worker role, and allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket for landing/. The statement also allows s3:PutObject for merged/ so the service can write consolidated files of roughly 256 MB. The role's account must allow the same actions, while the bucket policy supplies the cross-account permission. Set the service's target file size to 256 MB and its source prefix to landing/. Start a compaction run on one hour of data. Verify that the number of objects under merged/ is lower than under landing/ and that the total record count is unchanged.

This guide configures the DataGate validation service to read incoming files and write validation reports in a single account. The service runs as an IAM role named datagate-validator in account 111122223333. It checks files in the inbound/ prefix of the bucket partner-feeds, which is in that same account. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket for inbound/. Add s3:PutObject for reports/ so the service can write one JSON report per validated file. The bucket policy is not changed, because the role's identity-based policy is the only mechanism granting access. Set the validation rules to require a schema match and a non-empty file. Upload a malformed test file to inbound/ and run the validator. Confirm that a report listing the schema error is written to reports/ with the same base name as the input file.

This guide configures the DataGate validation service to read incoming files and write validation reports across accounts. The service runs as an IAM role named datagate-validator in account 111122223333. It checks files in the inbound/ prefix of the bucket partner-feeds, which is owned by account 444455556666. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement naming arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/datagate-validator as the principal, allowing s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket for inbound/. The statement also allows s3:PutObject for reports/ so the service can write one JSON report per validated file. The role's own account must permit these actions as well, but the bucket policy carries the grant on the bucket. Set the validation rules to require a schema match and a non-empty file. Upload a malformed test file to inbound/ and run the validator. Confirm that a report listing the schema error is written to reports/ with the same base name as the input file.

This guide gives the TableShip export service access to read table snapshots and write CSV exports in one account. The service runs as an IAM role named tableship-export in account 111122223333. Snapshots are stored under the snapshots/ prefix of the bucket warehouse-snapshots, which is in the same account. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket for snapshots/. Add s3:PutObject for exports/csv/ so the service can write one CSV file per table. Do not modify the bucket policy; the role's policy alone provides the required permissions. Configure an export job with a snapshot identifier and set the output prefix to exports/csv/. Run the job for a table of about one million rows. Verify that the CSV row count equals the snapshot row count and that the object is readable only through the role.

This guide gives the TableShip export service access to read table snapshots and write CSV exports when the bucket belongs to another account. The service runs as an IAM role named tableship-export in account 111122223333. Snapshots are stored under the snapshots/ prefix of the bucket warehouse-snapshots, which is owned by account 444455556666. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement that names the tableship-export role ARN as the principal and allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket for snapshots/. The statement also allows s3:PutObject for exports/csv/ so the service can write one CSV file per table. The role's account must permit the same actions, and the bucket policy supplies the grant across the account boundary. Configure an export job with a snapshot identifier and set the output prefix to exports/csv/. Run the job for a table of about one million rows. Verify that the CSV row count equals the snapshot row count and that the object is readable only by principals the bucket policy allows.
